states.description: External, runtime, cache, bootstrap, or diagnostic input has been normalized into the shared architecture vocabulary before semantic branching.
Exactly one semantic owner and owner boundary has been selected for the normalized concern.
The selected owner has either authoritative evidence or a typed missing, deferred, blocked, or failed dependency outcome.
The owner emits one canonical outcome with contractState, nextAction, owner-specific evidence, and reason vocabulary.
Any owner-managed durable transition has been persisted through the owner path before observers consume it.
A durable owner transition that requires follow-up work has an atomic, recoverable, or replayable wake before observers depend on the transition.
Events enqueue owner-key work or projection work with typed reasons; no long-running progression executes inline.
Observer projection has a current owner epoch or observed-generation fence before readiness, admission, or progress is promoted.
Read models, diagnostics, admin views, harness reports, or caches project the owner outcome without becoming a second authority.
Temporary phase scaffolding has handed off to the steady-state runtime owner or the existing steady-state owner remains active.
Missing owner dependencies, blocked readiness, or failed evidence emit typed fail-closed owner outcomes instead of allow-by-default behavior.

transitions.evidence: Architecture single-owner rules and current owner maps identify one owner boundary for the normalized concern.
The owner reads canonical rows, declared read models, runtime authority, or typed dependency gaps instead of caller-local fragments.
The owner emits a ready or pending owner-contract outcome with a single nextAction and reason vocabulary.
Typed blocked, failed, or deferred outcomes prevent missing evidence from upgrading readiness or admission.
Owner-managed fields and lifecycle state change only through the owner writer or coordinator path.
Owner transitions that require follow-up work have a recoverable owner-key wake, replayable queue record, or equivalent outbox before observers depend on them.
The owner outcome is terminal or self-contained and requires no retry, projection, or handoff wake.
CDC, cache, diagnostics, admin, and reconcile events enqueue typed owner-key work instead of running progression inline.
Projection consumers compare observed epoch or generation with the owner outcome before readiness or admission decisions are promoted.
Observers project the canonical owner outcome and preserve its grammar instead of recomputing the semantic decision.
Bootstrap, join, recovery, and temporary phase owners transfer live responsibility to an explicit runtime owner before completion.
No phase handoff is required because the selected steady-state owner remains the only authority.

forbiddenTransitions.reason: Runtime logic consumes normalized state and must not reopen raw storage, transport, cache, bootstrap, or wire shapes.
Callers submit intent to owners; they do not reproduce owner logic locally.
Degraded or cross-plane evidence may explain or defer, but must not upgrade a blocked entity to ready or admitted.
Readers, caches, diagnostics, and harness consumers observe owner state; non-forced readers do not repair authoritative state on the hot path.
Committed owner follow-up work must not strand behind a lost wake or un-replayable projection transition.
Stale observer projections cannot promote readiness, admission, or owner progress.
Bootstrap, join, and recovery phases must not remain the steady-state owner after the phase completes.

invariants.statement: Every state transition, lifecycle decision, data transformation, cache view, diagnostic grammar, and runtime resource has exactly one semantic owner.
Runtime logic consumes normalized state and does not reopen raw storage, transport, bootstrap, cache, or wire shapes.
An owner emits one canonical outcome before observers, caches, diagnostics, admin views, or harness reports project the result.
Reader-local caches, diagnostics, and reports do not repair or replace authoritative owner state on the hot path.
Degraded or cross-plane evidence can explain, defer, or block, but cannot upgrade readiness or admission.
Temporary bootstrap, join, recovery, and migration owners transfer responsibility to explicit steady-state owners before phase completion.
A stale observer projection cannot promote readiness, admission, or owner progress across handoff boundaries.
Every durable owner transition that requires follow-up work has an atomic, recoverable, or replayable wake before observers depend on it.
